title: Runtime Observability Data Model and Tracebook
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Overview

This page defines the canonical telemetry/trace data model for the Redwood serving runtime, and collects pragmatic recipes (the "Tracebook") for diagnosing common kernel-scheduling and runtime-performance incidents. The goal is a single reference that: (1) standardizes events/labels emitted by runtime components, (2) specifies trace/span correlation conventions, and (3) provides step-by-step debugging playbooks for triaging GPU/CPU contention, KV-cache hotlines, and kernel fallback behavior.

Scope

- Components: dispatcher, rserv (user-level runtime), k-scheduler, kvcache-shard, loader, trace-collector.
- Signals: traces (OpenTelemetry), metrics (Prometheus), kernel events (perf/kern logs), GPU-side counters (NVIDIA DCGM where available).
- Not in scope: application-level prompts, customer PII, non-runtime business metrics.

Key principles

1) Consistent IDs: every request must carry request_id, route_id, and shard_id tags.
2) Lightweight single-sample events: emit small structured events at scheduling boundaries rather than large stack dumps.
3) Correlatable traces: attach source=client and model_variant labels to spans.
4) Dual-plane visibility: metric-derived alerts (SLOs) and trace-first investigations (root-cause).

Canonical fields (string keys emitted on spans/metrics)

| Field | Type | Meaning | Example |
|-------|------|---------|---------|
| request_id | string | Global request UUID injected at ingress | req_2026-03-01_7f3a |
| route_id | string | API route or customer route identifier | route:chat-completion-v2 |
| model_variant | string | Model identifier + quantization tag | gptj-16k-q8_0 |
| shard_id | string | Serving shard identifier (node:gpu index) | shard-usw2-12:gpu3 |
| kernel_path | string | Kernel execution path annotation | attention/sharded_fused |
| sched_policy | string | Scheduling policy used | preemptive/priority-bucket |
| kv_cache_hit | boolean | Hit/miss indicator for prefix cache | true |
| queue_time_ms | number | Time waiting to enter GPU queue | 4.2 |
| exec_time_ms | number | Kernel execution duration on GPU | 1.8 |
| fallback_reason | string | Why a fallback path executed | quant_conv_unavailable |

Trace/span conventions

- Tracer: OpenTelemetry (OTel) format. All internal services must use the Redwood OTel SDK wrapper which ensures:
  - Sampling: adaptive sampling that retains all traces flagged by alert rules (see section below).
  - Exporter: to the internal trace-collector — endpoint: https://trace-collector.internal:4317.
  - Baggage: request_id, route_id, model_variant.

- Span hierarchy (recommended):
  - ingress.span (generated by dispatcher)
    - request.routing.span (route decision + model variant lookup)
      - k-scheduler.enqueue.span (time added to scheduling queue)
        - k-scheduler.schedule.span (scheduling decision, includes policy)
          - gpu.exec.span (kernel execution; attach kernel_path, exec_time_ms)
          - kvcache.lookup.span (if prefix cache involved)

Instrumenting kernel scheduling details

Attach the following attributes to k-scheduler spans: sched_policy, priority_bucket (0-7), preemptible (true/false), soft_deadline_ms, queue_time_ms. Use numeric buckets for quick aggregation: priority_bucket: 0 (lowest) .. 7 (highest).

Kernel event taxonomy

- Normal exec: kernel_path includes architecture and fused-op indicators (e.g., attention/axial_fused_fp16). exec_time_ms reflects wallclock time on GPU.
- Fallback exec: fallback_reason present; often accompanied by increased exec_time_ms and a kernel shim label (kernel_path: attention/fallback_cpu_sync).
- OOM/Retry: emit event oom_attempts (int) on gpu.exec.span and increment metric runtime.kernel.oom_attempts.

Metric naming and SLOs

- Metrics (Prometheus):
  - runtime.request.latency_p50_ms, runtime.request.latency_p95_ms, runtime.request.latency_p99_ms
  - runtime.kernel.exec_time_ms_bucket (histogram)
  - runtime.kvcache.hit_ratio (gauge by route/model)
  - runtime.scheduler.queue_time_ms_summary
  - runtime.kernel.fallback_count_total

- Example SLOs (for hosted API):
  - 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 300ms for short-text route (<=256 tokens).
  - kernel fallback rate < 0.5% per model_variant over 24h.
  - KV cache hit_ratio >= 0.70 for conversational workloads in dedicated pools.

Tracebook: triage recipes

1) Symptom: sudden spike in request p99 for route:chat-completion-v2
- Step 1: open dashboard -> route latency -> filter route_id=chat-completion-v2 and time range last 30m.
- Step 2: check metric runtime.scheduler.queue_time_ms_summary and runtime.kernel.exec_time_ms_bucket. If queue_time_ms increased sharply -> contention at scheduling layer.
- Step 3: search traces by route_id + tag priority_bucket. Run query: resource.attributes.route_id:chat-completion-v2 AND k-scheduler.enqueue.span.queue_time_ms:>50.
- Step 4a: If many traces show priority_bucket==0 and preemptible==true, check autoscaling and pool utilization (gpu-fleet dashboard). Action: temporarily raise priority for recent canary traffic or route to dedicated pool.
- Step 4b: If exec_time_ms increased while queue_time small, inspect kernel_path for fallback_reason and kernel metrics. Common causes: quantization kernel not available on this GPU driver build -> fallback to CPU. Open host logs /var/log/rserv/kernel-fallback.log.

2) Symptom: elevated kernel fallback_count_total for model_variant=gptj-16k-q8_0
- Step 1: grep traces: fallback_reason and kernel_path. Look for recurring reason strings (e.g., quant_conv_unavailable, fused_op_missing).
- Step 2: correlate with node labels: hardware_capability and driver_version. Query node exporter: node_gpu_driver_version{model_variant=~"gptj.*"}. If failure concentrated on specific driver range -> roll forward driver or pin compatible variant.
- Step 3: rollback plan: pin affected route to older model_variant or disable aggressive quantization profile in the route config (console -> model routing -> override quant_profile).

3) Symptom: KV cache hit_ratio drop for a customer on dedicated pool
- Step 1: examine kvcache.shard metrics: runtime.kvcache.hit_ratio by shard_id and route_id.
- Step 2: inspect shard placement: k8s label shard_affinity and rough cache_size usage. If one shard shows >80% eviction_rate, run cache diagnostics: curl http://kvcache-shard-$SHARD/diagnostics | jq .eviction_histogram.
- Step 3: mitigation: increase per-shard cache_size (config map: kvcache-shard.size_mb) or rebalance routes to spread hot prefixes.

Investigating GPU kernel stalls and preemption

- Signals to collect: long-running gpu.exec.span (> 10ms for small kernels), per-GPU utilization (DCGM: sm_util), power draw spikes, and GPU-side queue depths.
- Recommended command on onprem nodes: 
  - dcgmi dmon -e 0 -s 200ms --format csv > /tmp/gpu-dmon.csv
  - ncu --target-processes all --kernel-name-base demangled --sample 200ms (only in controlled debug environments)

- If kernel exec_time_ms is high but SM utilization low, suspect memory-bound ops or PCIe stalls. Check node dmesg for pci errors and nvidia-smi pmon.

Trace and metric retention and sampling policy

- Retention: spans retained for 30 days in trace-store for production; high-fidelity traces for flagged incidents kept for 90 days.
- Sampling: default 1% head-sampling, adaptive increase to 100% for traces that hit any of these conditions: runtime.request.latency_p99>2*SLO, any kernel.fallback_reason present, or runtime.kvcache.hit_ratio<0.4.

Alerting examples

- Alert: runtime-kernel-fallback-rate-high
  - Query: increase(rate(runtime.kernel.fallback_count_total[5m])) by (model_variant) > 0.005
  - Severity: P2
  - Runbook: follow Tracebook recipe 2 (fallback investigation) and open a ticket with infra if driver incompatibility suspected.

- Alert: scheduler-queue-growth
  - Query: increase(runtime.scheduler.queue_time_ms_summary{quantile=\"0.95\"}[10m]) > 50ms
  - Severity: P1 if sustained for >5m
  - Runbook: see Tracebook recipe 1. Consider emergency scaling or temporary routing to dedicated pools.

Implementation checklist for instrumenters

- [ ] Use Redwood OTel SDK wrapper and ensure request_id is propagated across RPCs.
- [ ] Emit the canonical fields on k-scheduler and gpu.exec spans.
- [ ] Attach lightweight numeric tags (priority_bucket) for efficient aggregation.
- [ ] Add a top-level metric runtime.kernel.fallback_count_total with label fallback_reason.
- [ ] Add unit-tests that assert span attribute presence in end-to-end integration tests (see test/observability/integration in repo).

Dashboard and queries (examples)

- Grafana panels to build:
  - Per-route latency waterfall: groups by queue_time_ms vs exec_time_ms.
  - Kernel fallback heatmap: model_variant x driver_version -> fallback_count_total.
  - KV cache occupancy and eviction rate by shard.

- Example PromQL: 
  - p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_request_latency_bucket{route_id=\"chat-completion-v2\"}[5m])) by (le))
  - fallback rate by model: increase(runtime_kernel_fallback_count_total[10m]) / increase(runtime_requests_total[10m])

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime ( observability squad )
- Oncall escalation: SRE -> runtime infra -> applied-ml (for model-specific regressions)

Appendix A: example trace JSON (OTel-like, trimmed)

{
  "traceId": "4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736",
  "spans": [
    {
      "name": "ingress.span",
      "attributes": {
        "request_id": "req_2026-03-01_7f3a",
        "route_id": "chat-completion-v2",
        "model_variant": "gptj-16k-q8_0"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "k-scheduler.schedule.span",
      "attributes": {
        "sched_policy": "preemptive",
        "priority_bucket": "3",
        "queue_time_ms": "72.4"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "gpu.exec.span",
      "attributes": {
        "kernel_path": "attention/fallback_cpu_sync",
        "exec_time_ms": "28.9",
        "fallback_reason": "quant_conv_unavailable"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Appendix B: quick CLI snippets

- Search traces in trace-collector (OTel query API):
  curl -sS -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -X POST https://trace-collector.internal:4318/api/traces/search -d '{"query":"resource.attributes.route_id:chat-completion-v2 AND resource.attributes.model_variant:gptj*"}' | jq .hits

- Inspect kvcache shard diagnostics:
  export SHARD=shard-usw2-12
  curl -sS http://kvcache-shard-$SHARD:8080/diagnostics | jq

- Spin a high-priority scheduling test (internal loadgen):
  rloadgen run --route chat-completion-v2 --qps 200 --priority 7 --duration 5m
